item.description:
Problem Statement

Organizations hold valuable knowledge across documents, support tickets, project wikis, chat conversations and other enterprise sources. Employees often struggle to find the right information quickly, and then have to switch to another system to act on it: raise a ticket, check stock, log a fault, update a record. This is especially true for field teams, plant and site staff, and regional teams who work away from a desk, are more comfortable in their own language than in English, and cannot stop to type.

Much of this knowledge is written in English, which creates a barrier for people who think and speak in regional languages or mix languages naturally. Important insights stay buried across systems, while employees lose time searching, piecing information together and manually carrying out the follow-up steps.

The opportunity goes beyond answering questions faster. A real-time voice agent can let employees ask in the language they actually speak, get a grounded answer, and trigger the next step through connected systems, all hands-free and in the flow of work.

What Participants Are Asked to Build

Build a real-time, voice-to-voice AI Knowledge & Decision Agent using native audio-to-audio capabilities of Gemini (such as the Gemini Live API on Google Cloud) that helps employees access organizational knowledge and act on it across multiple enterprise data sources.

The agent must be action-oriented, not a passive Q&A chatbot. It should handle natural spoken dialogue, including mid-sentence interruptions, regional accents and code-switched speech such as Hinglish or Tanglish. It should understand intent, retrieve and synthesize relevant knowledge (including content written in a different language from the question), respond in the user's language, and execute a real follow-up action in a connected system, such as a ticketing tool, inventory database, work-order system or CRM.

You may target any high-impact sector, for example Retail, eCommerce, Manufacturing, Tech & Media, Telecom, Professional Services, Life Sciences & Healthcare, Fintech, Insurance, MSME Logistics, Field Services or Hospitality.

What You Decide to Build

You choose the industry, business challenge and use case. In your submission, define:

  1. Target User & Setting: Who uses your voice agent, and in what physical environment (plant floor, retail counter, vehicle, field site)?
  2. Operational Friction: What exact business bottleneck are you solving?
  3. Action Execution Path: How does spoken intent connect to retrieved knowledge and then to a database or API action?
  4. Commercial Viability: How does your solution create measurable, scalable ROI and hold up on unit economics at scale?

Key Capabilities

  • Native real-time voice experience: Voice as the primary interaction, with sub-second responses, natural turn-taking and smooth handling of mid-sentence interruptions. Text, documents, images or other modalities where they add value.
  • Vernacular and code-switched fluency: Understand questions asked in Indic languages, local dialects or mixed-language speech, and answer in the language the user prefers.
  • Cross-language retrieval: Retrieve and synthesize answers from sources written in a different language from the spoken query.
  • Multi-source enterprise knowledge: Connect documents, support tickets, wikis, chats and other relevant organizational sources.
  • Intelligent search and synthesis: Combine information from multiple sources into a coherent, useful spoken response.
  • Grounded action execution: Turn the answer into a downstream action, such as raising a ticket, checking or updating inventory, logging a fault, creating a work order or updating a record.
  • Trust and safety: Cite sources for verification and confirm important actions with the user (for example, a spoken read-back) before executing them.
  • Acoustic and field resilience: Maintain reliable understanding in noisy plant, field or on-the-move environments.

Expected Output

A functional prototype or agentic workflow that shows how Gemini can help users interact with and act on enterprise knowledge through real-time voice.

The demonstration should include:

  • A live voice interaction with natural turn-taking and at least one interruption.
  • At least one interaction in a language other than English, or in code-switched speech, ideally with realistic background noise.
  • A grounded response that shows how the input was understood and connected to relevant organizational information.
  • At least one real backend action triggered by the spoken request (a mocked system is acceptable).
  • Visible response latency.

Submissions should show measurable value and commercial viability, such as response latency, task completion rate, time saved finding information, answer accuracy, language coverage, and cost per resolved query or overall ROI at scale.

Optional Extension (Bonus)

Solutions may also show how knowledge, feedback or ideas spoken by employees can be captured and structured into the organization's knowledge base, or turned into personalized, shareable outputs. This is optional and is not required to qualify.
